title: Hybrid-order nonlinear topological phases
authors: Yu-Peng Ma, Ming-Jian Gao, Jun-Hong An
abstract: The bulk-boundary correspondence (BBC), which relates topological invariants to boundary modes, is well understood for linear systems but remains an open question in the presence of nonlinearity, where multigap topologies make the BBC obscure and the topological description troublesome. We address this by developing an auxiliary-system formalism that enables topological classification of nonlinear-eigenvalue systems. In the two-dimension (2D) case, we show that two fixed eigenvalues can harbor first-order gapless boundary modes and second-order corner modes. Stacking this 2D system along the third dimension (3D) reveals distinct hybrid-order realizations. Under uniform stacking, the corner states in the $xy$ plane transform into hinge states along the $z$ axis, yielding a 3D second-order phase, while the gapless boundary states become side-surface states, yielding a 3D first-order phase. For dimerized stacking, these states are further confined to the two ends of the $z$ axis, yielding a 3D third-order phase, and localized at the hinges, yielding a 3D second-order phase. Our results establish a multiband bulk-boundary correspondence and identify stacking engineering as a versatile platform for exploring hybrid-order topological phases in nonlinear systems.
summary: This paper tackles the challenge of applying bulk-boundary correspondence to complex nonlinear quantum systems. By developing an auxiliary system formalism, the authors successfully classify topological phases in 2D and demonstrate how stacking a 2D model into 3D can engineer distinct hybrid-order topological states, including third-order phases.
main_problem: The bulk-boundary correspondence (BBC) is poorly understood for nonlinear systems, especially those with multigap topologies, making topological description difficult.
main_result: The authors establish a multiband bulk-boundary correspondence and demonstrate that stacking engineering can realize exotic 3D hybrid-order topological phases (first-, second-, and third-order).
method: They develop an auxiliary-system formalism to map the nonlinear eigenvalue problem onto a formally linear pencil matrix, allowing for topological classification.
model_or_system: The study uses a two-dimensional (2D) spinless square-lattice model with two degrees of freedom per unit cell, which is then generalized to 3D via uniform or dimerized stacking along the third dimension.
key_observables: Topological invariants include the Chern number ($C_1$) and the mirror-graded winding number ($W_2$); boundary states are diagnosed by gapless modes ($\lambda=0$) and localized using the Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR).
important_parameters: Stacking parameters, such as $	ext{t}_1$ vs. $	ext{t}_2$ for dimerized stacking, determine the resulting order of the topological phase.
main_assumptions: The method relies on mapping the nonlinear problem to a formally linear auxiliary system ($P(\omega)$) and addresses multiple-gap topologies beyond previous single-gap studies.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the eigenvalue spectra under Open Boundary Conditions (OBC) showing coexisting first-order ($\omega=0$) and second-order ($\omega=-M-1$) boundary states, and analyze the auxiliary system spectrum to confirm topological invariants in 2D and 3D.
paper_structure: The paper first addresses the theoretical gap regarding nonlinear BBC using an auxiliary system formalism. It then analyzes the 2D case showing coexisting boundary/corner states, before extending the analysis to 3D stacking configurations (uniform vs. dimerized) to realize higher-order phases.
why_interesting: This work extends topological concepts from linear systems into nonlinear regimes using a robust mathematical framework, which is highly relevant for understanding exotic phenomena in photonics and condensed matter wave physics.
